draft.title: Culling and restocking
card: Culling removes animals from a population. Restocking adds animals to it. Both can be built into a matrix recurrence by using a matrix B.
The rule is S(n+1) = T × S(n) + B. Multiply by T first, then add B.
A positive entry in B restocks that state. A negative entry in B culls that state.
draft.remember: Multiply by T first, then add B: a negative entry culls and a positive entry restocks.

a.q: In S(n+1) = T × S(n) + B, what does a negative entry in B mean?
opts: Animals are culled from that state each step
Animals are restocked into that state each step
That state's chance of staying is negative
That state is left out of the model
a.why: B is added after the transition, so a negative entry takes that many away from the state. Restocking is the opposite, and it needs a positive entry.
a.clue: B is added to the population, so a negative number takes away.

b.q: Deer live in a forest and on a plain. Each year, T × S gives the new numbers after moving, where T = [0.8 0.1; 0.2 0.9]. Then B = [−20; 50] is added. At the start S(0) = [300; 200]. What is S(1), as forest then plain?
b.why: T × S(0) = [0.8×300 + 0.1×200; 0.2×300 + 0.9×200] = [260; 240]. Adding B gives [240; 290]. Adding B before multiplying by T gives 249 and 281, which is the wrong order.
b.clue: Find T × S(0) first, then add B to the result.

a.best: Animals are culled from that state each step

check.summary: No problems found. T × S(0) = [260; 240], and adding B gives [240; 290]; the distractors match common errors such as leaving out T or adding B first.

final.title: Culling and restocking
card: Culling removes animals from a population. Restocking adds animals to it. Both can be built into a matrix recurrence by using a matrix \(B\).
The rule is \(S_{n+1} = TS_{n} + B\). Multiply by \(T\) first, then add \(B\).
A positive entry in \(B\) restocks that state. A negative entry in \(B\) culls that state.
final.remember: Multiply by \(T\) first, then add \(B\): a negative entry culls and a positive entry restocks.

a.q: In \(S_{n+1} = TS_{n} + B\), what does a negative entry in \(B\) mean?
opts: Animals are culled from that state each step
Animals are restocked into that state each step
That state's chance of staying is negative
That state is left out of the model
a.why: \(B\) is added after the transition, so a negative entry takes that many away from the state. Restocking is the opposite, and it needs a positive entry.
a.clue: \(B\) is added to the population, so a negative number takes away.

b.q: Deer live in a forest and on a plain. Each year, \(TS_{n}\) gives the new numbers after moving, where \(T = \begin{bmatrix} 0.8 & 0.1 \\ 0.2 & 0.9 \end{bmatrix}\). Then \(B = \begin{bmatrix} -20 \\ 50 \end{bmatrix}\) is added. At the start \(S_{0} = \begin{bmatrix} 300 \\ 200 \end{bmatrix}\). What is \(S_{1}\), as forest then plain?
b.why: \(TS_{0} = \begin{bmatrix} 0.8 \times 300 + 0.1 \times 200 \\ 0.2 \times 300 + 0.9 \times 200 \end{bmatrix}\), which is \(\begin{bmatrix} 260 \\ 240 \end{bmatrix}\). Adding \(B\) gives \(\begin{bmatrix} 240 \\ 290 \end{bmatrix}\). Adding \(B\) before multiplying by \(T\) gives 249 and 281, which is the wrong order.
b.clue: Find \(TS_{0}\) first, then add \(B\) to the result.
